description: Set the contact persistence flag for contacts in the specified range. When persistence is set to 'on' (true), contacts will not be automatically deleted by the contact detection system regardless of relative motion between contacting pieces. This prevents contact deletion even when pieces separate beyond normal detection distance. Note that if one piece is deleted, the contact is deleted regardless of persistence flag state. The persist flag is off by default. For contacts in non-mechanical processes, setting persistence on also sets persistence on for corresponding mechanical contacts. By default, only mechanical contacts are considered.

parameters.flag: True to enable persistence, False to disable

methods.returns: True if contact persists, False otherwise

notes: Python SDK requires iteration over contacts - cannot set persistence for all contacts in one call
Command interface is more efficient for bulk persistence setting
Use range specification in command interface to avoid Python iteration

6.0: Live 6.0 grammar: the optional process selector precedes the subcommand ('contact mechanical <sub>' / 'contact thermal <sub>'); it is not a keyword of the subcommand itself.
7.0: Live 7.0 grammar: the optional process selector precedes the subcommand ('contact mechanical <sub>' / 'contact thermal <sub>'); it is not a keyword of the subcommand itself.
9.0: Live 9.7 grammar: the optional process selector precedes the subcommand ('contact mechanical <sub>' / 'contact thermal <sub>' / 'contact fluid <sub>' - fluid is 9.x-new); it is not a keyword of the subcommand itself.

examples.description: Set persistence flag on for all contacts (from official example). Use case: Prevent automatic contact deletion throughout simulation.
Make contacts in 'permanent' group persist. Use case: Ensure specific contacts remain even when pieces separate.

examples.command: contact persist on range contact type 'ball-ball'
examples.description: Make all ball-ball contacts persist. Use case: Track ball-ball interactions even after separation.
Restore normal deletion behavior for all contacts. Use case: Allow contact detection system to delete separated contacts.

examples.command: contact persist true range model linearpbond
examples.description: Make linearpbond contacts persist. Use case: Keep bond contact records even after bond breakage and separation.

examples.command: contact persist on mechanical range contact active
examples.description: Make all active mechanical contacts persist. Use case: Preserve contact network for analysis.
Disable persistence for contacts in specific spatial region. Use case: Allow normal deletion in specific zone.
